title: Silhouette
hook: The sung chorus line of the Naruto Shippuden opening: a stepwise D F# E figure that climbs to a G, then the B A D, B A D leaps and the D C# D E F# D tag

source.page: derived transcription of the second sung line of the chorus (recording 56.1-65.9 s)

evidence.summary: Derived transcription (SHA-256 6e70fd8edd5f54b2a62bbb37016f0e7933f59944f1cbbd624b5a3f9a903ccd7d) of the 27-note chorus line. Pitch order and onsets from the Kjy falling-note roll (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kjy-TQqtKYs), compared event by event with the 6h71 roll (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6h71uYUVRSg; 24 paired attacks, 3 documented absent attacks) and audited note by note against the original recording (KANA-BOON official upload https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dlFA0Zq1k2A, clip kept, SHA-256 bfd7341cfee64ae04db65a661684ce91e3ffcbcd5cebc026303be48fb9c5e52f): harmonic-salience audit of the lead vocal on a center-panned extraction and a band-passed mix; 26/27 notes have the expected pitch class first in at least 68% of frames, all 27 first or second in at least 80%; the second sung statement (27 more notes) reproduces the order except two variants the audio itself shows. Octave decisions: the leaps B and A are B4 and A4 (salience at 493 and 440 Hz exceeds the octave below by 14-24 dB; pyin reports B3/A3 octave errors).

title: Kanashimi wo Yasashisa ni
hook: The sung chorus of Naruto opening 3: the repeated B B B C# B A# figure that falls to F# and climbs back to A#, a lower D# E answer, and the restatement closing on a held B

source.page: derived transcription of the first chorus (TV-size recording 55.2-69.0 s)

evidence.summary: Derived transcription (SHA-256 745f5e7fd90409b82e38cdce2a1c3b2b9593640db9d87168e18dfc1288d3ed8b) of the 38-note chorus: pitch order and rhythm from the single-voice iMelodica Pianika tutorial lit-key roll (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8rw37vEdvRs, roll SHA-256 b90b23c11a283c46de07177dc1f2e4b3d80bd09ac334e00d514c8880ebed4005), audited note by note against the original recording (Crunchyroll TV-size upload https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9TOWvpAhu4g, clip kept, SHA-256 c670d3000fc503fd002e465186991dd268be2fb110da24db709b696eea4295ce): per-note harmonic-salience audit on a center-panned extraction and a band-passed mix, 35/38 notes first-ranked in at least 68% of frames and all 38 first-ranked for at least 80 ms; every attack has a detected audio onset within 0.12 s; the repeated A# A# (roll lines 134-135, 154-155) shows two attacks (audio onsets 58.76 s and 66.37 s). The tutorial staff notation confirms the rhythm. Octave: the audio pitches are the tutorial labels (B4, A#4, F#4).

corpus.notes: No original clip or alignment audit.

title: Birds of a Feather
hook: The sung chorus: a rising answer to the held opening tone, then the same figure with a sixteenth turn, a repeated high B-A figure and a stepwise fall

evidence.summary: Primary: Hooktheory public JSON (SHA-256 1e191768685e06ad91db709429a387879c5adc9f2e6b248892b2f7da70cb34e1), D major, 105 BPM, one key, 74 notes, frozen as a derived MIDI. Reference: my pitch-track transcription of the lead vocal of the original recording (official lyric-video audio, first chorus 60.3-95 s; original clip kept, SHA-256 eaf29dba33e2c81cd3470ad18d89b71208d7d0ef30369baca76851d0830879a2): 54 attacks matched as same-pitch pitch-track events within 0.2 s of the 105 BPM grid (class A), 17 pitch-present positions adjudicated from the contour (class B) and 3 positions without usable pitch evidence kept as documented absent rows (class C: notes 8, 20 and 33). Audio absolute pitch agrees with the Hooktheory octave (no shift). Medium confidence: onsets agree only within 0.5 beat after a constant offset, the lead vocal was read from a mixed recording without stem separation, and the reading was made with the Hooktheory positions in view. No listening review.

corpus.notes: No original clip or alignment audit.
